criteria.substantial: Multiple specific and independently examined source passages sufficient to teach main question and counterarguments
criteria.developing: Specific site/date evidence supports a focused explanation but essential questions remain
criteria.sparse: A few preliminaries, description or abstracts insufficient for responsible treatment
criteria.missing: No meaningful subject evidence in inspected corpus

cells.review_basis: Institutional descriptions specify the 1900 electric tram to Tacubaya and 1891 animal-drawn versus 1900 electric tram service toward Tlalpan; still lacks route maps, operator records, fare structures and independently checked opening dates.
cells.scope: Web abstracts and INAH page, not original timetables

cells.review_basis: UNAM teaching page provides 1858 and 1910 area figures but does not define urban boundary or original calculation; cannot responsibly teach quantitative growth yet.
cells.scope: Teaching page only; no original cartography

cells.review_basis: INEHRM synopsis supplies February 9–23 Decena Trágica framing, but no claim-to-day or site-specific military chronology. Not yet sufficient for field walk.
cells.scope: Catalogue synopsis; book and contemporary sources not examined

cells.geography: Centro Histórico, former San Francisco convent
cells.review_basis: Monument catalogue identifies 1861 closure and later transfers, but the structural-survival inventory and ownership history remain single-source; duplicate-map previous 1861 claim before integration.
cells.scope: INAH web monument record; deed originals unexamined

cells.review_basis: Contemporary directive excerpt offers property-right and financing terms; earlier 1985 material records CUD formation and demands, allowing a provisional policy-versus-implementation comparison. Resident case studies and actual budgets missing.
cells.scope: Official directive excerpt and secondary scholarly material; no implementation audit

cells.review_basis: Period labor commentary and earlier staged union-formation research offer concrete chronology and workplace vulnerabilities; original factory records and individual testimonies remain unexamined.
cells.scope: Contemporary published abstract + prior staged research, no factory archives

cells.theme: housing damage statistics and methodological debates
cells.review_basis: 1986 article abstract contrasts several incompatible categories of loss; adequate to teach uncertainty itself, not to assert one definitive total or explain district distributions.
Single later newspaper-content study identifies the reuse of 1985 disaster memory in 2017 reporting; no primary newspaper corpus or reception research examined.
